learningObjective: Reason about how functionalization treats an in-place update on a view (aliased mutation).

canonicalClaims.claim: AOTAutograd's functionalization models an in-place update on a view as a scatter-style update of the underlying tensor (`slice_scatter`, `select_scatter`, `index_put`), threading the new SSA value through downstream ops; the compiled region returns the mutated tensor so the runtime wrapper can preserve external mutation semantics.
conditions: The view has a supported representation (slice/index).
nonImplications: Does not imply every view+mutation pattern compiles equally well; unusual patterns can graph-break.
Does not imply the runtime write-back is free.

misconceptions.claim: Functionalization silently discards mutations on views.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It preserves them via scatter-style rewrites.

misconceptions.claim: AOTAutograd errors out on any view+mutation.
Mutations fall back to eager Python per op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: There is no per-op Python fallback; functionalization stays in the compiled graph.
Boundary bookkeeping (extra tensor return + write-back) has real cost.

implementationFacts: Common scatter ops: slice_scatter, select_scatter, index_put
Compiled region returns additional tensors for externally-observed mutated inputs
Runtime wrapper writes back mutated tensors onto the caller's tensors
performanceScenarios: Functionalization enables graph-level optimizations at the cost of extra tensor arguments and write-backs on the boundary.
